name: Enosh
overview: Enosh is a male figure in the early biblical genealogies, uniquely identified as the son of Seth. There is no tribal affiliation or additional notes provided about him. His role is primarily genealogical, linking the generations following Adam through Seth.
namesAndTitles: The name Enosh means '[mortal] man,' reflecting the human condition. This proper name is mentioned in Genesis 4:26 and was not given by God, indicating a common human name rather than a divine title.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Enosh as the son of Seth and the father of Kenan. These relationships situate him within the early lineage of mankind as presented in Genesis 4:26 and Genesis 5:9.
scriptureSignificance: Enosh holds significance as a key patriarch in the biblical genealogical record, bridging the line from Seth to subsequent generations. His mention marks the continuation of humanity after the fall, emphasizing the mortal nature of man as reflected in his name. Enosh’s place in Scripture underscores the unfolding of God's plan through successive generations, though no further narrative details are provided about his life or deeds.
